title: The rage of Caliban at not seeing his face in a mirror, he said. If Wilde were only alive to see you!
html_source:
Paraphrased from the preface to Oscar Wilde’s Dorian Gray:

The nineteenth century dislike of realism is the rage of Caliban seeing his own face in a glass.

The nineteenth century dislike of romanticism is the rage of Caliban not seeing his own face in a glass.

In Shakespeare’s play The Tempest, Caliban is a wildman, or man-fish, or beast-man inhabiting the desert island on which the principal characters are wrecked.

ACCEPTED COMMENT: Caliban lived peacefully on an island until foreigners arrived and subjugated him–here a possible analogy for England’s conquest of Ireland.
